comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, women represented 27.9% of global employees and 25.3% of technical positions, while underrepresented minorities comprised 17.8% of US employees and 8.7% of US senior leadership positions.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and INTC disclose specific Board and workforce diversity demographics. MU reports its Board composition as 5 men and 4 women, with one Asian, one African-American, and seven White members. INTC reports its broader workforce diversity, noting that in 2024 women represented 27.9% of global employees and underrepresented minorities (including Black/African American and Hispanic employees) comprised 17.8% of US employees. Both disclosures provide a breakdown of ethnic and gender representation within their organizations.

In addition, as of August 29, 2024, based on self-identification, one member of our Board of Directors is Asian, one member is African-American, and seven members are White.
In 2024, women represented 27.9% of our global employees, 18.3% of our senior leadership positions [footnote 2: Senior leadership is defined as salary grades 10+ or equivalent grades.
Population includes all regular Intel employees but does not include Mobileye and other non-integrated subsidiaries employees.] , and 25.3% of our technical positions.

Underrepresented minorities [footnote 3: Underrepresented minority population includes all regular Intel employees but does not include Mobileye and other non-integrated subsidiaries employees.] , including Black/African American employees, Hispanic, and Native American employees, represented 17.8% of our US employees and 8.7% of our US senior leadership positions.
